answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making fraud detection a bonded market. Any peer may accuse identities of being one controller, posting a bond as dear as saffron; a random jury of staked peers checks shared endpoints and timing, then a confirmed cluster is slashed and the accuser paid. A false charge forfeits the bond, so honest monitoring is cheap, lying costly. Each clone leaves a comet's tail of shared traces, and a gale of minting only swells the bounty a monitor claims. Flag, slash, expel keeps sanctions cheap. This caps cheap flooding, not a wealthy attacker who isolates clones.
